content.title: Forms Need Labels and Instructions
content.hook: Forms fail quickly when people do not know what a field means. Every form control needs a clear label, and unusual input rules need clear instructions.

content.title: Labels are not placeholders
content.text: A placeholder is temporary hint text inside a field. It should not replace a persistent label. The label tells the user what the field means even when the field is empty or after text has been entered.

content.title: Useful instructions
content.text:
```html

Use 6–20 letters or numbers.

```

content.question: A username must contain 6–20 letters or numbers. Which is the stronger instruction?

feedback.correct: Users should be told about constraints that affect how they can complete the field.
feedback.incorrect: Users should be told about constraints that affect how they can complete the field.

content.title: Grouping related choices
content.text: When several controls belong to one question, the page should make that relationship clear. For example, a small group of related choices should read as one question with clearly labeled choices.

content.title: Related choices
content.text:
```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Preferred contact method</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="contact" value="email"> Email</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="contact" value="sms"> SMS</label>
</fieldset>
```

content.question: What is the strongest form rule?

options.text: Make the fields look obvious and let users guess the rest.
Give each control a clear label and provide instructions for important constraints.
Use placeholder text instead of labels.
Hide all instructions until the user fails.

feedback.correct: Clear labels and instructions reduce uncertainty before the user submits anything.
feedback.incorrect: Clear labels and instructions reduce uncertainty before the user submits anything.
